decisions.executionNote: Approach the white correction tape with the left arm, raising and pitching its gripper downward gradually; right arm stays parked.
Use half-size increments after the unexecuted IK rejection, retaining the initial elbow branch.
Continue a slow elevated left-arm approach, progressively turning the fingers toward a top-down grasp.
Bring the open left gripper inward above the target while continuing its downward pitch; maintain overhead clearance.
Move closer above the tape with extra vertical clearance as the approach direction becomes downward.
Finish near-vertical approach orientation above the correction tape, keeping the fingers open and above its surface.
Align over the tape and turn the open jaws to span its narrow dimension rather than its long axis.
Continue rotating the open jaws above the tape without lowering; inspect narrow-axis alignment before descent.
Complete jaw alignment across the tape width and refine its overhead center before lowering.
Lower the aligned open gripper by 3 cm toward the tape, checking fingertip clearance and centering from RGB.
Descend another 2 cm slowly with jaws open to bring the pads beside the tape body.
Close the left jaws gradually around the tape at the current height; grasp retention remains to be verified visually.
Keep closing briefly, then perform a 1.5 cm test lift to check whether the correction tape follows the gripper.
The tape appears to follow the test lift in the wrist view. Continue lifting vertically with the gripper commanded closed.
The tape remains visibly retained. Raise another 6 cm to exceed the requested 10 cm lift with a small margin.
